# Serverpod documentation

> Serverpod is an open-source app server for the Flutter community, written in Dart. Every documentation page is also available as markdown at its page URL with `.md` appended. This index covers the current stable framework docs and the Serverpod Cloud docs.

## Framework documentation

- [Introduction](https://docs.serverpod.dev/index.md): Serverpod is an open-source backend framework for Flutter developers. Write your server in Dart and call it from your app through generated, type-safe code.
- [Installation](https://docs.serverpod.dev/installation.md): Prerequisites
- [Quickstart](https://docs.serverpod.dev/quickstart.md): Build and deploy a full-stack Flutter and Serverpod app, hosted on the web, in 10–15 minutes. We have tested the default setup with Antigravity, Cursor, and Claude Code, but most agentic editors will work.
- [How Serverpod works](https://docs.serverpod.dev/how-it-works.md): Start building with Serverpod. Learn how to add endpoints, call them from Flutter, define data models, and work with hot reload across the backend and your app.
- [Create your first endpoint](https://docs.serverpod.dev/get-started/creating-endpoints.md): Build a Serverpod endpoint that turns a list of ingredients into an AI-generated recipe with Gemini, and call it from your Flutter app.
- [Create data models](https://docs.serverpod.dev/get-started/models-and-data.md): Define a Serverpod data model so your endpoint returns typed, structured data, with serialization between server and client generated for you.
- [Manage the database](https://docs.serverpod.dev/get-started/working-with-the-database.md): Store your Serverpod recipes in the database with typed methods and migrations, so they persist between sessions and can be listed in your app.
- [Deploy your app](https://docs.serverpod.dev/get-started/deployment.md): Deploy your Serverpod recipe app to Serverpod Cloud with the Serverpod CLI, then explore other hosting options.
- [Serverpod Academy](https://docs.serverpod.dev/serverpod-academy.md): Free video course on the Serverpod framework. Build a complete app end-to-end and earn a certificate on completion.
- [Backend fundamentals](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tutorials/fundamentals.md): This video explains the fundamentals of backend development, how a database works, and how to get started with Serverpod. It is a great starting point for a Flutter developer new to working with backends and servers.
- [Real-time communication](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tutorials/real-time-communication.md): Have you ever found real-time communication in apps challenging? It doesn't have to be. Today, we're diving into how to build a collaborative drawing experience using Flutter and Serverpod. We'll call our app Pixorama - a fun and interactive project inspired by Reddit's r/place. Pixorama lets users draw together on a shared grid, with every pixel placed updating in real-time across all connected devices.
- [Integrating AI & RAG](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tutorials/ai-and-rag.md): Are you curious about how best to include AI in your Flutter app? In this talk, we will explore how you can use Serverpod to stream content generated by Gemini to your Flutter app in real-time. We will also dive into calling the Gemini APIs from Dart and linking them to your custom knowledge database using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and a vector database. We build a practical example where you can chat with the Flutter and Serverpod documentation, pulling in data from official docs, issues, and discussions on GitHub.
- [Support & community](https://docs.serverpod.dev/support.md): Welcome to the Serverpod community! We offer several ways to get help, stay informed, and connect with other developers.
- [Your Serverpod project](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/server-fundamentals/your-serverpod-project.md): A Serverpod project is one Dart workspace with three packages, the server, the generated client, and your Flutter app, plus its config and migrations.
- [Running your server](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/server-fundamentals/running-your-server.md): The serverpod start command runs your project in development, with code generation, hot reload, the database, migrations, and the Flutter app in one terminal.
- [Configuration](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/server-fundamentals/configuration.md): Configuration in Serverpod comes from YAML files, environment variables, or a Dart config object, with run modes, source precedence, and secrets.
- [Modules](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/server-fundamentals/modules.md): Serverpod modules are reusable packages that bundle server, client, and Flutter code with their own endpoints and database tables.
- [Working with endpoints](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis.md): Endpoints expose server methods to a generated, typed client your Flutter app calls, with one client setup pointed at each environment.
- [Sessions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/sessions.md): The Session object gives every endpoint call access to the database, cache, file storage, and messaging, and manages its own lifecycle and logging.
- [Error handling and exceptions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/error-handling-and-exceptions.md): Errors in Serverpod reach the app as serializable exceptions defined in model files, caught by type alongside typed HTTP failures.
- [Streaming](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/streaming.md): Streaming methods in Serverpod are endpoint methods that return or receive Dart Streams over a managed WebSocket, with typed exceptions across the wire.
- [Server events](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/server-events.md): Server events in Serverpod post messages to named channels through session.messages, delivered locally or across a cluster via Redis.
- [Caching](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/caching.md): A cache stores a result under a key so the next request can read it back, held in server memory or in Redis and reached through session.caches.
- [File uploads](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/file-uploads.md): File uploads in Serverpod go directly to storage via signed upload descriptions, with database, GCP, S3, and Cloudflare R2 backends.
- [Custom cloud storage](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/custom-cloud-storage.md): A custom CloudStorage that stores uploaded files on local disk or a NAS, while FileUploader keeps talking to your API server.
- [Endpoint inheritance](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/endpoint-inheritance.md): Endpoint inheritance lets one endpoint extend another, override behavior from Serverpod modules, and control which subclasses generate client code.
- [Backward compatibility](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/backward-compatibility.md): Backward compatibility keeps your Serverpod server working with older client versions through rules for endpoint signatures, model fields, and future calls.
- [Endpoint middleware](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/endpoint-middleware.md): Middleware on the API server intercepts endpoint requests and responses for concerns such as logging, caching, and rate limiting.
- [Configure HTTP calls](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/endpoints-and-apis/configure-http-calls.md): HTTP transport for the generated client is configurable through httpClientOverride, for CORS credentials on web and native network stacks.
- [Working with models](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/models.md): Serverpod model files define serializable classes, exceptions, and enums, with fields, defaults, visibility, and generated Dart code.
- [Field types](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/models/field-types.md): Maps every Serverpod YAML field type to Dart, Postgres, SQLite, and JSON, including defaults, query operators, and storage caveats.
- [Inheritance and polymorphism](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/models/inheritance-and-polymorphism.md): Model inheritance defines class hierarchies with extends and sealed, uses polymorphic types in endpoints, and handles unknown subtypes across client versions.
- [Dynamic fields](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/models/dynamic-fields.md): Store values of varying types in Serverpod models using dynamic fields, with serialization and database support for JSON and JSONB columns.
- [Custom serialization](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/models/custom-serialization.md): Custom serialization passes your own classes through Serverpod endpoints and models with toJson/fromJson, Freezed, and ProtocolSerialization.
- [Shared packages](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/models/shared-packages.md): Shared packages in Serverpod define models usable in both server and client code, depending only on serverpod_serialization with no server-only dependencies.
- [Tables](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/tables.md): Table models map serializable classes to database tables in Serverpod, with custom ID types, non-persistent fields, JSONB storage, and column name overrides.
- [CRUD](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/crud.md): The generated db methods on each model class create, read, update, upsert, and delete database rows in Serverpod, in single-row and batch variants.
- [Filter](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/filtering.md): Database filter expressions in Serverpod are type-safe, built from column operations, logical operators, and relation filters.
- [Sort](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/sorting.md): Serverpod sorts query results by one or more columns with orderBy and orderByList, including relational fields and aggregated counts.
- [Pagination](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/pagination.md): Serverpod paginates large query results with limit and offset, or with cursor-based pagination for frequently updated datasets.
- [Relations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations.md): Database relations in Serverpod link rows across tables with foreign keys, in one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many, and self-referencing shapes.
- [One-to-one](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/one-to-one.md): A one-to-one relationship links two tables through Serverpod's relation keyword, with object fields, ID fields, and bidirectional access.
- [One-to-many](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/one-to-many.md): A one-to-many relationship links a parent row to many child rows through Serverpod's relation keyword, with implicit and explicit options.
- [Many-to-many](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/many-to-many.md): A many-to-many relationship connects multiple records on each side through a junction model that holds foreign keys to both tables.
- [Self-relations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/self-relations.md): A self-referential relationship points a table's foreign key back to its own primary key, supporting one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many patterns.
- [Referential actions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/referential-actions.md): Referential actions control how updates and deletes propagate across related tables through the onUpdate and onDelete properties.
- [Deferrable constraints](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/deferrable-constraints.md): Deferrable foreign key constraints move the constraint check from the end of each statement to the end of the transaction, so rows can be written in any order.
- [Relations with modules](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relations/modules.md): Module relations connect your own database tables to tables from Serverpod modules, such as the auth module's users, through a bridge table.
- [Relation queries (Joins)](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/relation-queries.md): Relation queries in Serverpod fetch, filter, sort, and paginate related data through include, includeList, attach, and detach methods.
- [Vector & geography fields](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/vector-and-geography-fields.md): Vector and geography fields store high-dimensional embeddings with pgvector and geospatial data with PostGIS in Serverpod models.
- [Indexing](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/indexing.md): Indexes on Serverpod database tables improve query performance, including unique, GIN, HNSW, and IVFFLAT vector indexes.
- [Transactions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/transactions.md): Transactions group database operations into an atomic unit in Serverpod, with isolation levels, savepoints, and rollback.
- [Row locking](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/row-locking.md): Row locking holds specific database rows within a transaction in Serverpod, so concurrent updates do not conflict.
- [Raw access](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/raw-access.md): Serverpod's unsafe query methods run raw SQL directly against the database, with named and positional parameter binding.
- [Migrations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/migrations.md): Database migrations keep your Serverpod schema in sync as your models evolve, with repair migrations to recover a database that has drifted out of sync.
- [Connection](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/connection.md): The database connection is defined in Serverpod's configuration and password files, with support for custom Postgres or SQLite instances.
- [Runtime parameters](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/runtime-parameters.md): Runtime parameters tune PostgreSQL query behavior per transaction or globally in Serverpod, notably for vector similarity search.
- [Client-side database](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/client-side-database.md): The client-side database runs SQLite on the Flutter client with the same ORM interface as the server, including CRUD, relations, and transactions.
- [Database exceptions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/exceptions.md): Serverpod wraps database failures in typed exceptions that signal when a query fails and how your code should handle it.
- [Database interceptors](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/database-interceptors.md): A database interceptor replaces session.db once per session with a custom database layer for tracing, policy enforcement, and tenant scoping.
- [Embedded PostgreSQL](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/data-and-the-database/database/embedded-postgres.md): Embedded PostgreSQL is a real PostgreSQL server that Serverpod starts and stops with your server, for local development and testing without Docker.
- [Get started with authentication](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/get-started.md): Authentication is built into every new Serverpod project. Turn on the sign-in screen, run your app, and test signing up and signing in.
- [Set up the authentication module](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/setup.md): Authentication in Serverpod is provided by the serverpod_auth_idp module. Install and configure it to add user management and sign-in to your project.
- [Authentication basics](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/basics.md): Authentication tokens are handled automatically by Serverpod. Learn how to access the signed-in user from the Session object.
- [Working with users](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/working-with-users.md): Authenticated users have a stable identifier across your server. Access them and their profile data from the Session object.
- [Set up anonymous sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/anonymous/setup.md): Anonymous authentication lets users access your app without creating an account. Enable it in your Serverpod auth configuration to get started.
- [Customize anonymous sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/anonymous/customizations.md): Configuration options and UI customizations for the anonymous identity provider, including app attestation tokens, rate limiting, and the AnonymousSignInWidget and AnonymousAuthController.
- [Set up email sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/email/setup.md): Sign in with Email lets users authenticate with an email and password, with verification codes delivered by Serverpod Cloud or your own email provider.
- [Configure email sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/email/configuration.md): Email identity provider options include password peppering and other security settings. Configure them beyond the basic setup.
- [Customize the email sign-in UI](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/email/customizing-the-ui.md): Email sign-in UI can be customized with the EmailSignInWidget and EmailAuthController to build a custom authentication flow.
- [Email admin operations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/email/admin-operations.md): Email admin operations manage email accounts and clean up expired or dangling verification requests through the EmailIdpAdmin server-side API.
- [Set up Google sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/google/setup.md): Sign in with Google requires Google Cloud OAuth credentials. Create them for your platforms and add the provider to your Serverpod app.
- [Customize Google sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/google/customizations.md): Configuration options for Google sign-in, including GoogleIdpConfig callbacks on the server, client IDs and redirect URIs in the app, sign-in button customization, and custom UIs with GoogleAuthController.
- [Google admin operations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/google/admin-operations.md): Use GoogleIdpAdmin from server-side code to look up Google-backed accounts and to link a Google identity to an existing Serverpod user.
- [Troubleshoot Google sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/google/troubleshooting.md): Sign in with Google failures, from setup mistakes to platform-specific errors, and how to diagnose and resolve each one in your Serverpod app.
- [Set up Apple sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/apple/setup.md): Sign in with Apple requires Apple credentials and platform setup. Register them and add the provider to your Serverpod app across iOS, macOS, Android, and web.
- [Customize Apple sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/apple/customizations.md): Configuration options for Sign in with Apple, including AppleIdpConfig credentials and web routes, app build variables, and UI customization with AppleSignInWidget and AppleAuthController.
- [Apple admin operations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/apple/admin-operations.md): Use AppleIdpAdmin from server-side code to check Sign in with Apple accounts and to handle accounts that Apple has already revoked.
- [Troubleshoot Apple sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/apple/troubleshooting.md): Sign in with Apple failures, from setup mistakes to OAuth response errors, and how to diagnose and resolve each one in your Serverpod app.
- [Set up Facebook sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/facebook/setup.md): Sign in with Facebook uses a Facebook Login app and an extra provider package. Create the app and add the provider to your Serverpod app.
- [Customize Facebook sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/facebook/customizations.md): Configuration options for Facebook sign-in, including FacebookIdpConfig callbacks, app-side App ID setup, and UI customization with FacebookSignInWidget and FacebookAuthController.
- [Troubleshoot Facebook sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/facebook/troubleshooting.md): Sign in with Facebook failures, from the JavaScript SDK toggle to iOS tracking permission and Android key hashes, and how to diagnose and resolve each one.
- [Set up Firebase authentication](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/firebase/setup.md): Firebase authentication connects any Firebase sign-in method to your Serverpod backend and syncs the authenticated user with a server-side session.
- [Configure Firebase authentication](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/firebase/configuration.md): Firebase identity provider credentials can be loaded from different sources with FirebaseIdpConfig. Configure the provider beyond the basic setup.
- [Customize the Firebase authentication UI](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/firebase/customizing-the-ui.md): Firebase authentication UI is built on the firebase_auth package and synced with your Serverpod backend through the FirebaseAuthController.
- [Firebase admin operations](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/firebase/admin-operations.md): Firebase admin operations manage Firebase-authenticated accounts from secure server-side code through the FirebaseIdpAdmin.
- [Troubleshoot Firebase authentication](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/firebase/troubleshooting.md): Firebase authentication failures when using Firebase with Serverpod, with the cause of each one and the steps to diagnose and resolve it.
- [Set up GitHub sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/github/setup.md): Sign in with GitHub uses OAuth2 credentials from a GitHub App. Register the app and add the provider to your Serverpod app.
- [Customize GitHub sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/github/customizations.md): Configuration options for GitHub sign-in, including credential loading, server callbacks, app-side client IDs, and custom UIs built with GitHubSignInWidget and GitHubAuthController.
- [Troubleshoot GitHub sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/github/troubleshooting.md): Sign in with GitHub failures, from setup mistakes to OAuth callback errors, and how to diagnose and resolve each one in your Serverpod app.
- [Set up Microsoft sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/microsoft/setup.md): Sign in with Microsoft uses a Microsoft Entra ID app registration. Create it and add the provider to your Serverpod app.
- [Customize Microsoft sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/microsoft/customizations.md): Microsoft identity provider options beyond the basic setup, from tenant and account validation on the server to client IDs and a custom sign-in UI in the app.
- [Troubleshoot Microsoft sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/microsoft/troubleshooting.md): Sign in with Microsoft failures, from setup mistakes to token exchange errors, and how to diagnose and resolve each one in your Serverpod app.
- [Set up passkey sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/passkey/setup.md): Passkey sign-in adds passwordless authentication to your Serverpod backend using the WebAuthn and FIDO2 standards for phishing-resistant logins.
- [Custom providers](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/custom-providers/overview.md): Custom identity providers plug your own sign-in method into Serverpod's authentication module, next to the built-in providers, with the same tokens, sessions, and user handling.
- [Set up the OAuth2 utility](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/custom-providers/oauth2-utility/setup.md): The OAuth2 utility provides PKCE helpers to integrate any OAuth2-compliant provider without handling the low-level protocol yourself.
- [Create an OAuth2-based identity provider](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/providers/custom-providers/oauth2-utility/creating-an-oauth2-based-identity-provider.md): A complete, working custom OAuth2 identity provider built with Serverpod's OAuth2 utility, ready to adapt for your own provider.
- [Managing tokens](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/token-managers/managing-tokens.md): Token managers issue, validate, revoke, and list authentication tokens in Serverpod. Learn how they work and how to access them.
- [JWT token manager](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/token-managers/jwt-token-manager.md): The JwtTokenManager provides stateless JWT authentication with short-lived access tokens and refresh token rotation. Configure it on the server.
- [Server-side sessions token manager](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/token-managers/server-side-sessions-token-manager.md): The ServerSideSessionsTokenManager provides database-backed sessions with immediate revocation and inactivity timeouts. Configure it on the server.
- [Authentication UI components](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/ui-components.md): The SignInWidget is an all-in-one sign-in UI that detects the providers you configured. Control which providers it shows, style its buttons, and translate its texts.
- [Manage user profile photos](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/profile-photos.md): User profile photos are handled by the authentication module and served from public storage. Expose the upload endpoint, display photos in your app, and configure image size, format, and storage.
- [Set up authentication on macOS](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/macos-authentication.md): Add the macOS Keychain Sharing entitlement your Flutter app needs so Serverpod authentication sessions persist after sign-in, including email and social providers.
- [Set up authentication on the web](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/web-authentication.md): Keep web sign-in tokens in httpOnly cookies so JavaScript can never read them, with server configuration, client setup, CORS implications, and local development notes.
- [Custom authentication overrides](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/custom-overrides.md): Custom authentication overrides let you implement your own handling when the serverpod_auth_idp module does not fit your requirements.
- [Set up the legacy auth module](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/setup.md): The legacy serverpod_auth module adds email and social sign-in to existing Serverpod projects. Install and configure it on the server and client.
- [Legacy authentication basics](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/basics.md): Authentication tokens in the legacy serverpod_auth module are handled automatically. Learn how to access the signed-in user from the Session object.
- [Working with users](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/working-with-users.md): User information in the legacy serverpod_auth module is read and updated through the Users class. Learn how to work with signed-in users.
- [Email sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/providers/email.md): Sign in with Email in the legacy serverpod_auth module connects Serverpod to an SMTP service for email and password sign-in.
- [Google sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/providers/google.md): Sign in with Google in the legacy serverpod_auth module uses Google credentials added to your app and server across iOS, Android, and web.
- [Apple sign-in](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/providers/apple.md): Sign in with Apple in the legacy serverpod_auth module is supported on iOS and macOS, including in development with an Apple Developer subscription.
- [Firebase authentication](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/providers/firebase.md): Firebase authentication in the legacy serverpod_auth module uses Firebase UI auth to add social sign-in methods Serverpod does not support directly.
- [Custom providers](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/providers/custom-providers.md): Custom providers in the legacy serverpod_auth module let you implement your own authentication and connect users with auth tokens.
- [Custom authentication overrides](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/authentication/legacy/custom-overrides.md): Custom authentication overrides in the legacy serverpod_auth module let you implement your own handling when its providers do not fit your needs.
- [Overview](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/overview.md): Serverpod's built-in web server serves REST APIs, webhooks, static files, server-rendered HTML, and Flutter web apps alongside the API server.
- [Routing](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/routing.md): Routing in Serverpod's web server supports HTTP method filtering, path parameters, wildcards, fallback handling, and virtual host routing.
- [Request data](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/request-data.md): Request data in Serverpod's web server is accessible via Relic's type-safe accessors for path parameters, query parameters, headers, and the request body.
- [Web server middleware](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/web-server-middleware.md): Middleware in Serverpod's web server lets you apply cross-cutting concerns like authentication, logging, and CORS globally or to specific path prefixes.
- [Static files](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/static-files.md): Static file serving in Serverpod supports automatic content-type detection, cache control headers, cache-busting, and conditional request handling.
- [Server-side HTML](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/server-side-html.md): Server-side HTML rendering in Serverpod uses WidgetRoute with Mustache templates or Jaspr components, with full access to the database.
- [Single-page apps](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/single-page-apps.md): Single-page apps in Serverpod use SpaRoute to serve the app's static files and fall back to index.html so client-side routing works.
- [Flutter web apps](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/web-server/flutter-web.md): Flutter web app serving in Serverpod uses FlutterRoute with SPA-style fallback, revalidation-based caching, and optional WASM headers.
- [Overview](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/scheduling/overview.md): Future calls schedule work to run later, on a delay, at a set time, or on a repeating schedule, persisted in the database so they survive restarts.
- [Future calls](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/scheduling/future-calls.md): A future call is a method Serverpod runs later, scheduled after a delay or at a specific time, and cancellable by identifier.
- [Recurring tasks](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/scheduling/recurring-tasks.md): A recurring task runs a future call on a repeating schedule, set with callRecurring using either a fixed interval or a cron expression.
- [Inheritance](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/scheduling/inheritance.md): FutureCall inheritance shares methods between classes, exposes a module's future calls through an abstract base, and allows overrides.
- [Configuration](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/scheduling/configuration.md): Future call settings cover execution, concurrency, the scan interval, and broken-call handling, set in config files or environment variables.
- [Overview](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/overview.md): Operations covers running Serverpod in production through logs, health checks, TLS, exception monitoring, and scaling past a single process.
- [Logging](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/logging.md): Serverpod records a log entry for calls, queries, and your own messages, stores them in the database or prints them to the console, and can purge old entries.
- [Health checks](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/health-checks.md): Serverpod answers liveness, readiness, and startup probes at /livez, /readyz, and /startupz, supports custom health indicators, and collects health metrics about itself.
- [Security and TLS](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/security-and-tls.md): How traffic to a Serverpod server is encrypted, when something else handles that for you, and how to serve HTTPS directly from the server instead.
- [Exception monitoring](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/exception-monitoring.md): Diagnostic event handlers report exceptions from your code and from the framework to a monitoring service as they happen.
- [Scalability](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/scalability.md): Scaling guidance for Serverpod: server roles, isolates for CPU work, Postgres indexes and pools, Redis, JWT auth, and when short RPCs beat long-lived streams.
- [Redis](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/redis.md): Redis connection setup for Serverpod: enabling it, the host, port, and password, the development Docker instance, and connecting a GUI such as RedisInsight.
- [Load testing](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/operations/load-testing.md): Load testing for Serverpod: concurrent traffic from Locust or the generated client against a production-like server, read through Insights, logs, and Postgres.
- [Get started with testing](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/testing/get-started.md): The Serverpod test tools call your endpoints like ordinary Dart functions, running a real server and a real database that resets between tests.
- [Writing tests](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/testing/writing-tests.md): The pieces every Serverpod test uses, the session builder, simulated authentication, seeding the database, and the exceptions the test tools throw.
- [Configuration](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/testing/configuration.md): Every option withServerpod accepts, including run mode, database rollback behavior, server output, timeouts, and test tags.
- [Advanced examples](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/testing/advanced-examples.md): Advanced Serverpod testing examples, separate unit and integration runs, test business logic, shared streams, future calls, and exception monitoring.
- [Best practices](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/testing/best-practices.md): Best practices for Serverpod integration testing, import only the generated test tools file, rely on automatic database rollback, and always call endpoints through the provided endpoints object.
- [Introduction to the Serverpod CLI](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/introduction.md): The Serverpod CLI reference. Every command, with the global options and environment variables that apply across all of them.
- [Global options](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/global_options.md)
- [CLI environment variables](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/env_vars.md): These environment variables affect the serverpod command:
- [serverpod cloud](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/cloud.md)
- [serverpod completion](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/completion.md)
- [serverpod create](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/create.md)
- [serverpod create-migration](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/create-migration.md)
- [serverpod create-repair-migration](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/create-repair-migration.md)
- [serverpod database](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/database.md)
- [serverpod generate](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/generate.md)
- [serverpod language-server](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/language-server.md)
- [serverpod mcp-server](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/mcp-server.md)
- [serverpod quickstart](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/quickstart.md)
- [serverpod run](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/run.md)
- [serverpod start](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/start.md)
- [serverpod upgrade](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/upgrade.md)
- [serverpod version](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/cli/commands/version.md)
- [Configuration reference](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/lookups/configuration-reference.md): Every Serverpod configuration option, covering run settings, server and service ports, database, Redis, session logs, future calls, and code generation.
- [Model reference](https://docs.serverpod.dev/concepts/lookups/model-reference.md): Every keyword available in Serverpod model files, with a note on each and which of class, exception, and enum the keyword applies to.
- [Deploy to Serverpod Cloud](https://docs.serverpod.dev/deployments/deploy-to-serverpod-cloud.md): Deploy your Serverpod Flutter backend to Serverpod Cloud in minutes, with zero configuration, a managed database, and TLS.
- [Choosing a strategy](https://docs.serverpod.dev/deployments/custom-hosting/choosing-a-strategy.md): Choose how to self-host a Serverpod server, on a server cluster, a serverless platform, or your own machine, as an alternative to Serverpod Cloud.
- [Hosting elsewhere](https://docs.serverpod.dev/deployments/custom-hosting/hosting-elsewhere.md): Run Serverpod on any host that supports a Dart process or a Docker container, with notes on required services, configuration, server roles, and Docker.
- [Community-supported deployments](https://docs.serverpod.dev/deployments/custom-hosting/community-supported.md): Community-built tools for deploying Serverpod, including a CLI for deploying to a VPS with Docker-Compose. Not officially maintained.
- [Serverpod Insights](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tools/insights.md): Serverpod has a companion app. It is currently available for Mac and Windows, but Linux is coming soon. The app has support for viewing your server's logs and health metrics, but we are adding many more features in version 1.2. You must use a version of the app that matches the version of Serverpod you use in your project, or not all features may work correctly.
- [LSP server](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tools/lsp.md): The Serverpod language server gives editors diagnostics, go to definition, and find references for model files, via the VS Code extension or the LSP command.
- [Run scripts](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tools/run-scripts.md): The serverpod run command allows you to define and execute custom scripts from your pubspec.yaml. This is useful for common tasks like starting the server, running tests, or building executables.
- [Command line completion](https://docs.serverpod.dev/tools/shell-completion.md): As a serverpod user, you can enable command line completion in most shells. The Serverpod CLI supports completion through Carapace, which provides tab-completion for commands, options, and their values in bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell, and more.
- [Upgrade to 4.0](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/upgrade-to-four.md): Upgrading a Serverpod 3.4 project to 4.0 (Jetstream) brings serverpod start, the embedded Postgres option, and the new agent skills.
- [Upgrade to 1.2](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/upgrade-to-one-point-two.md): Serverpod 1.2. is backward compatible with Serverpod 1.0 and Serverpod 1.1. There are a few changes to the database layer, meaning you probably want to use the new methods. The old methods still works, but have been deprecated and will be permanently removed with the upcoming version 2.
- [Upgrade to 2.0](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/upgrade-to-two.md): Changes to authentication
- [Upgrade from Mini to full](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/upgrade-from-mini.md): If you have started with Serverpod Mini, you can upgrade to the full Serverpod version anytime. Before you upgrade, it's good practice to back up your project, as some configuration files can be overwritten if you have manually created them.
- [Upgrade to 2.2](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/upgrade-to-two-point-two.md): Serverpod 2.2 includes new test tools that make it easy to create tests for endpoint methods. For new projects they are configured by default, but existing projects need to go through some steps to enable it (see below). The full documentation of this feature can also be found here.
- [Upgrade to pgvector](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/upgrade-to-pgvector.md): New Serverpod projects automatically included pgvector support through the pgvector/pgvector PostgreSQL Docker image. From 4.0.0-beta.2, the compose file uses ghcr.io/serverpod/postgres:16 instead, which is that image plus PostGIS. Existing projects need to be upgraded to use vector functionality.
- [Upgrade to 3.0](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/upgrade-to-three.md): The new authentication module has separate migration documentation. This guide covers only core framework changes.
- [Streaming endpoints (removed in 4.0)](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/archive/streaming-endpoints.md): The streaming endpoints API removed in Serverpod 4.0 (streamOpened, handleStreamMessage, openStreamingConnection). Use streaming methods instead.
- [Migrate from legacy serverpod_auth](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/migrate-from-legacy-auth.md): Upgrading from serverpod_auth_server to the new modular auth stack while email users keep their passwords and existing sessions keep working.
- [Upgrading to PostGIS support](https://docs.serverpod.dev/upgrading/upgrade-to-postgis.md): Add PostGIS to a Serverpod project to enable geography fields, with steps for Docker, managed PostgreSQL services, and pgvector.
- [Roadmap & contributions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/contribute.md): Serverpod is built by the community, for the community. We believe the best software comes from collaboration, where many people contribute their ideas and skills. That's why we strive to make contributing as easy as possible and share our plans for future development in our public roadmap.

## Serverpod Cloud documentation

- [Introduction](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud.md): Serverpod Cloud is a managed hosting platform for Serverpod apps. Deploy from the command line; Cloud manages runtime, networking, database, and secrets.
- [Set up the Cloud CLI](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/getting-started/installation.md): Run the Cloud CLI through the Serverpod CLI or install it on its own, then authenticate it with your account.
- [Deploy your first app](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/getting-started/launch.md): Run serverpod cloud launch to create a Cloud project, deploy your Serverpod server, and open it at a public URL. Takes about five minutes.
- [Deployments](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/deployments.md): Deploy your Serverpod app to Cloud, check deployment status, validate packages before deploying, and control what's included in the deployment.
- [Logs](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/logs.md): How Serverpod Cloud surfaces logs through Insights, the Serverpod Cloud CLI for terminal access and filtering, and session-log configuration.
- [Passwords, secrets, and environment variables](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/passwords-secrets-env-vars.md): Serverpod Cloud has three configuration tiers: encrypted passwords via the Serverpod API, encrypted secrets as named env vars, and plaintext variables.
- [Custom domains](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/custom-domains.md): Custom domains attach to the web, API, or Insights surface of a Serverpod Cloud project, with automatic TLS and DNS-based verification.
- [Database](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/database.md): How Serverpod Cloud's managed PostgreSQL works, including provisioning, automatic server credentials, migrations on deploy, backups, user access, and resetting the database.
- [Database backups](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/database-backups.md): Database backups on Serverpod Cloud are point-in-time snapshots of the managed database, taken on demand or on a schedule and restorable in one step.
- [Personal access tokens](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/personal-access-tokens.md): Create personal access tokens to authenticate the Serverpod Cloud CLI in CI pipelines, scripts, and headless environments without interactive login.
- [Content delivery and caching](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/cdn.md): The Serverpod Cloud CDN serves your app's cacheable static content from the edge nearest each user and clears its cache automatically on every deploy.
- [Deployment hooks](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/concepts/deployment-hooks.md): Run custom scripts at fixed points in a Serverpod Cloud deploy. Pre-deploy hooks handle setup like code generation; post-deploy hooks send notifications.
- [Use Redis for PubSub and caching](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/guides/redis.md): Configure a third-party Redis service like Upstash for distributed caching and PubSub across multiple Serverpod Cloud server instances.
- [Ship non-Dart files with your server](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/guides/ship-non-dart-files.md): Include configuration files, templates, data, or other non-Dart assets alongside your Serverpod Cloud server and read them at runtime.
- [Deploy from CI with GitHub Actions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/guides/deploy-from-ci-with-github-actions.md): Use the official serverpod_cloud_deploy GitHub Action to deploy your Serverpod Cloud project on every push to your main branch.
- [Recover from a failed deploy](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/guides/recover-from-a-failed-deploy.md): Diagnose why a deploy to Serverpod Cloud failed, read the build log, identify the failure type, and ship a fix to recover without disrupting any running version.
- [Dart SDK versions](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/dart-sdk-versions.md): Which Dart SDK versions Serverpod Cloud supports, and how to select the version your deploy builds with using the --dart-version flag, scloud.yaml, .tool-versions, or your pubspec constraint.
- [Private dependencies](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/private-dependencies.md): How to deploy a Serverpod Cloud project that depends on private packages, using Dart workspaces or build secrets for private git repositories.
- [Project identifier rules](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/project-id-rules.md): Naming rules for the Serverpod Cloud project identifier and how the Cloud CLI picks which project to operate on: scloud.yaml, -p flag, or environment variable.
- [scloud.yaml schema](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/scloud-yaml-schema.md): The schema for scloud.yaml: every key, its type, what the Cloud CLI preserves across commands, and the validation errors you might see.
- [Introduction to the scloud CLI](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/introduction.md): The Serverpod Cloud CLI (scloud) reference. Every command, with the global options and environment variables that apply across all of them.
- [Global options](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/global_options.md)
- [CLI environment variables](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/env_vars.md): The scloud command supports a number of environment variables, many of which
- [scloud auth](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/auth.md)
- [reference/cli/commands/build/build](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/build.md)
- [scloud completion](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/completion.md)
- [scloud db](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/db.md)
- [scloud deploy](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/deploy.md)
- [scloud domain](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/domain.md)
- [scloud help](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/help.md)
- [scloud launch](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/launch.md)
- [scloud log](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/log.md)
- [scloud me](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/me.md)
- [scloud password](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/password.md)
- [scloud project](https://docs.serverpod.dev/cloud/reference/cli/commands/project.md)
